chunks: From him, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The hand of the thief is not cut off except for an item whose value reaches a Mijann, and it is a quarter of a Dinar.

key_terms.دِينَارٍ: Dinar, a gold coin used as a standard of value
key_terms.مِجَنًّا: A Mijann, a specific unit of currency/value

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum value of stolen goods required for cutting the thief's hand in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the nisab (minimum value) for hadd al-sariqah, specifying that the stolen item must be worth at least a Mijann, defined here as a quarter of a Dinar. This threshold ensures that the severe corporal punishment is reserved for significant theft, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on proportionality and the protection of the accused from minor infractions. The definition of Mijann as a quarter dinar highlights the specific economic standards used by the Imams to determine legal liability in their time.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The hand of the thief would not be cut regards to anything except if it reaches the value of a Mijanna, and it is a quarter of a Dinar’.
